title: A Simple Hanging Drop Cell Culture Protocol for Generation of 3D Spheroids
protocol: Grow adherent cell cultures to 90% confluence.
Rinse monolayers twice with PBS.
Add 2 mls of 0.05% trypsin-1 mM EDTA and incubate at 37°C until cells detach.
Stop trypsinization by adding 2 mls of complete medium.
Triturate the mixture gently until cells are in suspension.
Transfer cells to a 15 ml conical tube.
Add 40 μl of a 10 mg/ml DNAse stock and incubate for 5 minutes at RT.
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 200 XG for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant and wash pellet with 1 ml complete tissue culture medium.
Repeat washing step.
Resuspend cells in 2 mls of complete tissue culture medium.
Count the cells using a hemacytometer or automated cell counter.
Adjust concentration to 2.5 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Remove lid from a 60 mm tissue culture dish and place 5 mls of PBS in the bottom as hydration chamber.
Invert the lid.
Use a 20 μl pipettor to deposit 10 μl drops onto the bottom of the lid.
Ensure that drops are placed sufficiently apart so they do not touch.
Invert the lid onto the PBS-filled bottom chamber.
Incubate at 37°C/5% CO2/95% humidity.
Monitor drops daily to assess aggregate formation.
Use a stereo microscope to check for aggregate formation.
Transfer cell sheets to round-bottom glass shaker flasks containing 3 mls of complete medium once they form.
Incubate in a shaking water bath at 37°C and 5% CO2 until spheroids form.
